articles.title: ‘Yellowjackets’ joins the best shows on streaming this week
articles.description: The Streamable’s experts rank the top shows currently available to stream today. Just about everything in the television and entertainment industries has changed in the past five to 10 years. Not too long ago, the month of September was focused almost exclusively on the return of football and the launch of a new, robust slate of TV shows. However, as cord-cutting rapidly decreased the number of Americans watching television in traditional ways, the release calendar has shifted. So while there are still a number of new and returning shows premiering on broadcast channels during the back half of the month, it is nowhere near the numbers of decades past. Many of the best titles on TV have migrated from networks and cable channels to streaming in recent years, but with the non-standard release schedules, it can be tough to keep up with what is airing where and when, and which shows are actually worth watching. So, as your guide to all things streaming, the experts here at The Streamable are providing you with an easy-to-navigate list of the top 11 shows currently on streaming and how you can watch them. Take a look at the list below — and how we determine the shows represented — and figure out what you are going to be watching tonight! All about The Streamable’s top-11 shows on streaming list: For those who are new to this list, the basic rules are that, in order to be eligible, a show must be a streaming exclusive or premiere episodes on streaming before or on the same day as they air on linear channels. Shows that air episodes weekly are eligible for inclusion until one week after their season finale. For series that drop all episodes at once, they are eligible for one full week per episode. For full rules and methodology, click here. The top 11 titles are listed in order of how long they are eligible for inclusion, from shortest to longest. What are the top 11 shows on streaming right now? updated November 27, 2026 A high school girls’ soccer team crash-landing in the wilderness and being forced to survive for 19 months is about as high-concept a premise I can imagine. That’s “Yellowjackets” in a nutshell, except you also get to see the lives of the survivors 25 years later, and just how much those months have tortured them for decades. Now, I’ve always loved the soccer team’s storyline more than the adult segments, just because of the intensity and the sheer desperation of their situation. And now, in the final season of “Yellowjackets,” the girls are coming home. But integrating back into society isn’t going to be as easy as it seems. And how do these girls actually keep quiet about the horrific things they did out there? I’m very curious to see how the PTSD manifests with their families, friends, and everyone else so happy to have them home. And hopefully, we’ll get some real answers as to whether what they did and saw was really supernatural or just a collective fever dream for survival. New episodes drop every Friday on Paramount+ through Jan. 22. Top streaming TV shows for the week of November 27, 2026 ‘Phony’ Season 1 | Hulu | Eligible Until Dec. 8, 2026 Phony October 20, 2026 After waking up from a freak car accident, Sonny discovers that his mother has been replaced by an impostor. ‘Crystal Lake’ Season 1 | Peacock | Eligible Until Dec. 10, 2026 Crystal Lake October 15, 2026 Single mother Pam Voorhees has been unable to shake her grief after her young, sickly son Jason tragically drowned in the town lake almost a year before. When two strangers arrive at Pam’s door digging into her past, a disturbing chain of events is set into motion, leaving the townspeople of Crystal Lake wondering: just who is Pam Voorhees? ‘The Diplomat’ Season 4 | Netflix | Eligible Until Dec. 10, 2026 The Diplomat April 20, 2023 Amid an international crisis, a US diplomat contends with her high-profile job as ambassador to the UK and her strained marriage to a political star. ‘The Terminal List’ Season 2 | Prime Video | Eligible Until Dec. 16, 2026 The Terminal List June 30, 2022 Navy SEAL Commander James Reece turns to vengeance as he investigates the mysterious forces behind the murder of his entire platoon. Free from the military’s command structure, Reece applies the lessons he’s learned from nearly two decades of warfare to hunt down the people responsible. ‘The Good Daughter’ Season 1 | Peacock | Eligible Until Dec. 24, 2026 The Good Daughter November 12, 2026 Sisters Charlotte and Samantha Quinn have spent the last twenty-eight years trying to piece together the lives that were fractured by a single night of violence. When another attack splinters the small town of Pikeville, Charlotte is the first witness on the scene. Now a lawyer like her father, she’s forced to confront her own demons as the case twists through one shocking revelation after another. In the end, both she and Samantha find themselves wondering if the price of being the good daughter was worth it after all. ‘Nobody Wants This’ Season 3 | Netflix | Eligible Until Dec. 31, 2026 Nobody Wants This September 26, 2024 An agnostic sex podcaster and a newly single rabbi fall in love, but can their relationship survive their wildly different lives and meddling families? ‘North of North’ Season 2 | Netflix | Eligible Until Dec. 31, 2026 North of North January 7, 2025 A young Inuk woman wants to build a new future for herself after a spontaneous and extremely public exit from her marriage. It won’t be easy in a small Arctic town where everybody knows your business. ‘Nocturne’ Season 1 | Apple TV | Eligible Until Jan. 1, 2027 Nocturne October 29, 2026 When a victim of notorious serial killer Jurek Walter unexpectedly turns up alive, detective Jonah Lynn races against time to find the one person still missing, while his protégé Saga Bauer goes undercover to get answers from the killer himself. ‘Stick’ Season 2 | Apple TV | Eligible Until Jan. 6, 2027 Stick June 3, 2025 Pryce Cahill was headed for golf greatness when an on-course meltdown derailed his career. Now struggling to stay afloat, he goes all in to mentor Santi—a teenage phenom with immense potential—and maybe save himself. ‘The Body’ Season 1 | Netflix | Eligible Until Jan. 6, 2027 The Body November 11, 2026 After a dance-team initiation gone wrong, a group of badly behaved Catholic school girls begin having prophetic visions that set off mass hysteria in their town. ‘Yellowjackets’ Season 4 | Paramount+ | Eligible Until Jan. 29, 2027 Yellowjackets November 14, 2021 This equal parts survival epic, psychological horror story and coming-of-age drama tells the saga of a team of wildly talented high school girls soccer players who become the (un)lucky survivors of a plane crash deep in the remote northern wilderness. The series chronicles their descent from a complicated but thriving team to savage clans, while also tracking the lives they’ve attempted to piece back together nearly 25 years later. How do you determine what is considered a streaming show? The lines between streaming and cable are blurring more than ever as media companies begin to line up premiere days and times for all of their outlets and even drop episodes on streaming before they are available on traditional linear channels. So, for our purposes, we will count any show that is available on a streaming service on the same day and time as it is on its broadcast or cable channel. If an episode premieres on HBO on Sunday night at 9 p.m. ET and it is also available on HBO Max at the same time, then it counts as a streaming show. However, if it first airs on Bravo on Tuesday but isn’t available on Peacock until Wednesday morning, then, unfortunately, it does not qualify for our list. How long does a show remain eligible for this list? With streaming services deploying different release strategies for different titles, we realize that there needs to be some sort of guidelines to make sure that every series has a fair shake. So, for shows that release episodes weekly, obviously, they will be available through the week following their season finale. For series that drop all of their episodes at once — either for a full season or in parts — they will get as many weeks as they make episodes available. So, if Netflix releases eight episodes of a new season, it will get eight weeks of eligibility for The Streamable’s Top-10 List. How do you determine which shows are the best? Obviously, there is no definitive, objective measure of artistic quality. So, we will use a sampling of available review metrics from Reelgood, Rotten Tomatoes, IMDb, and others, as well as our own finely-tuned opinions.
